title: Shaving Foam & Bubbles
strapline: Light, whippy, disappearing foam — pure sensory joy.
intent: Foam and bubbles are irresistible and low-stakes: there is nothing to make and no way to fail, so every child can dive in.
Swirling, patting and smoothing foam is a big, satisfying surface for mark-making with fingers and whole hands.
Whisking, pouring and popping bubbles is a fine-motor and cause-and-effect playground.
The changing, disappearing nature of foam and bubbles invites noticing, predicting and wondering.
It's a wonderfully calming, sociable, side-by-side activity that draws children into shared talk.
implementation: Spread foam straight onto a tuff tray or table so there is a big surface to draw and write in.
Add whisks, bowls, bubble wands and a little colour so there's plenty to explore.
Get your own hands in alongside — model swirling, patting and drawing shapes and letters.
Name what's happening: 'The bubbles are getting bigger... pop! Where did that one go?'
Invite mark-making: draw a line, a circle, the first letter of a name, then wipe and start again.
Ask real wondering questions about the changes: 'What do you think will happen if we whisk it harder?'
Keep it a free exploration — the point is the process, not a product.
key_questions: How does the foam feel — can you make it into a pattern?
What happens to the bubbles when you touch them?
How could you make more bubbles, or bigger ones?
Can you draw a shape — or the first letter of your name — in the foam?
Where do you think the foam goes when it disappears?

impact.text: Children swirl, pat and smooth the foam, exploring the material freely with hands and fingers.
Children make marks, lines and early shapes in the foam and talk about them.
Children whisk, pour and pop bubbles, refining finger control and hand strength.
Children notice and predict what happens as the foam and bubbles change and disappear.
Children become calmly absorbed and share the experience happily alongside others.
Children describe the sensations — soft, wet, fluffy, slippery — building sensory vocabulary.

enhancements: Whisks, hand-mixers, bowls and spoons for whipping up more.
Bubble wands, bubble snakes (a sock over a bottle) and a bubble machine.
A little liquid watercolour or food colouring to swirl and mix.
Letter and number cards to copy into the foam.
Small-world animals or vehicles to wash and hide in the foam.
A mirror underneath the tray for foam prints and reflections.

playing_exploring: Children plunge into an inviting, no-fail material and use their senses fully.
They test what happens as they whisk, poke, smear and pop.
active_learning: Children stay happily with the foam, repeating and refining what their hands can do.
creating_thinking: Children predict what the foam and bubbles will do and try out ways to make more or bigger.
